Sustainable Hydrocarbon Fuels Research — Landscape Report

498 papers · 2001–2022 · generated 2026-03-31 22:57

Corpus of 498 open-access, English-language papers from OpenAlex covering sustainable fuels (biofuels, SAF, HVO, FT fuels, conventional hydrocarbon fuels and related feedstocks) intersected with environmental or performance impact topics (emissions, efficiency, combustion properties, lifecycle analysis). A sub-sample of 498 papers has been further classified by a large language model (LLM) to characterise research scope and ML/AI usage.

4. AI / ML in sustainable-fuels research

498 papers in this corpus have been classified by the LLM batch pipeline. The analysis below answers how and where machine learning is applied in the field — covering research scope, learning paradigms, model classes, and growth trends.

Key findings:
  • 2% of classified papers employ at least one ML/AI method, indicating the field is in a rapid AI-adoption phase.
  • The dominant research scope is fuel_production, engine_testing, emissions_reduction.
  • supervised is the most common ML paradigm, with evolutionary the most frequent model class.
  • Papers span CFD simulations, experimental studies, and data-driven property prediction — often combining multiple modelling approaches.

Research scope distribution

Each paper may fall into one or more research categories. Engineering design optimisation and fuel property prediction are the most active areas where ML/AI techniques are being applied.

ML/AI adoption rate

What fraction of sustainable-fuels papers use any ML/AI method? The pie shows the overall split; the time-series tracks how this share has changed year-on-year.

Learning paradigm and model class

Among papers that do use ML/AI, the breakdown below shows which paradigms and model families are most prevalent. Supervised learning dominates — driven by property-prediction and regression tasks — while deep learning is gaining ground for combustion-image and time-series applications.
